race_name: Nordic Chase Copenhagen to Oslo Road

top_categories.workout_context: 451 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.

Road-specific control matters at Nordic Chase Copenhagen to Oslo Road. Practice on rolling three-country point-to-point road ultra: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 451 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Nordic Chase Copenhagen to Oslo Road's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before race day.
At Nordic Chase Copenhagen to Oslo Road, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
17,060ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Nordic Chase Copenhagen to Oslo Road's rolling three-country point-to-point road ultra rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
451 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 451 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 17,060ft of climbing on rolling three-country point-to-point road ultra does to your power file on race day.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Nordic Chase Copenhagen to Oslo Road. Train it until it feels boring.
Low-cadence force work supports 17,060ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Nordic Chase Copenhagen to Oslo Road. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.

race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 451 miles: 80–100g carbs/hour from mile 1 — don’t wait until you’re hungry. Practice your exact race-day nutrition in every long training ride. Carry backup calories. 451 miles burns 8,000–12,000+ calories — you cannot replace them all, but you must try.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Nordic Chase Copenhagen to Oslo Road rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on rolling three-country point-to-point road ultra to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Road Specific, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 451 miles of rolling three-country point-to-point road ultra in Copenhagen, Denmark to Oslo, Norway.
